chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Ayyūb, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, that he said:
For the tongue of the mute, the eye of the blind, and the penis of the free castrated man and his two testicles, there is one-third of the diyah.

key_terms.اَلدِّيَةِ: the prescribed blood-money or legal financial compensation for injury
key_terms.اَلْأَخْرَسِ: the mute person, one who cannot speak
key_terms.اَلْأَعْمَى: the blind person, one lacking sight
key_terms.عَيْنِ: the eye, as an organ in the law of bodily injury
key_terms.لِسَانِ: the tongue, as an organ for which legal compensation is assessed

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for the tongue of a mute person, the eye of a blind person, and the sexual organ of a free castrated man in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning compensation for injury to certain organs whose function is already impaired or altered. It assigns one-third of the diyah in these specified cases within the laws of bodily injury compensation.
